transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Well, thanks for seeing me. I guess what brings me in is... I just feel like I’ve got a motor humming right under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like when I'm in staff meetings at work, or sitting through church event briefings. I just can't stay put. I always end up shifting around in my chair, standing up, or just finding some excuse to get up and move around.
Have you had this restlessness since childhood?

Yeah, pretty much as long as I can remember. I mean, I remember getting in trouble back in grade school for popping out of my seat all the time. I'd end up talking over the teacher, or... I'd just rush ahead on things before the directions were even finished. My mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even as a kid. So, yeah, it's definitely been going on since then.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

No, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I mean, sure, if there's a real problem, like an unexpected bill or something, I'll think about it. But I don't just sit around worrying about things for no reason. My mind is usually jumping from one thing to the next too fast to get stuck on worrying.
Do you also have trouble paying attention when you need to focus?

No, not really. I mean, I don't have a problem focusing on my work. As a building cleaner, I know what needs to be done and I just do it. I might do it fast, and I might jump from mopping to taking out the trash and back again, but I get it all done. I don't sit there spacing out or forgetting what I'm supposed to be doing. My problem is more about just needing to keep moving, not about losing my focus.
When you feel that urge to keep moving, do you actually feel uncomfortable or distressed if you try to sit still?

No, it's not really like a... like a pain or anything distressing. It's just more of an itch, you know? If I'm sitting down for too long, I just feel like I need to get up and stretch my legs or do something with my hands. I don't feel anxious or upset about it, I just... I just prefer to be on the move.
Do other people usually notice you as fidgety or constantly on the move?

Yeah, they definitely notice. On my shifts, I'm always going from mopping to checking the trash, then over to straightening chairs, without really stopping. I just keep moving. And my family sees it too, because even at home... well, instead of just sitting down to rest after work, I'll usually head out and start puttering in the garage, or maybe re-sorting my tools. I just stay active like that.
When you’re moving around, does it feel like you’re driven to move even when you don’t want to, or is it more that you choose to stay busy?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I don't think I feel forced to move, like against my will or anything. I just... I guess I just choose to stay busy. It feels normal to me to keep doing things. I haven't really stopped to think about whether it's some kind of drive or just me wanting to get stuff done. I just do it.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on details or making careless mistakes when you’re doing tasks?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, my job is mostly details—getting the corners clean, making sure the supplies are stocked right. I don't really make careless mistakes with that stuff. I might move fast, but I get it done right. I don't really have a problem focusing on what I'm doing.
When you feel like you need to move around, do you feel tense or anxious inside if you try to stay still?

Yeah, I do. Actually, that's kind of what brought me in to see you. If I'm supposed to just sit still—like in our staff meetings at work, or during briefings for church events—I start feeling like I've got a motor humming right under my skin. 

I don't know if I'd call it anxious, but it's definitely tense. I just can't sit there. I always end up shifting around in my chair, or I'll just stand up in the back of the room, or I'll find some excuse to step out and move around for a minute.
Does this restlessness happen even when you’re relaxed and comfortable, or only when you’re feeling tense or stressed?

It happens even when I'm relaxed, honestly. Like, if my wife and I go fishing, or if we go to bingo... I'm supposed to be relaxing, but I catch myself tapping my foot, or messing with my tackle box, or playing with the bingo pencil. I end up talking too loud, too. It just gets hard for me to just sit there, be quiet, and actually enjoy the downtime.
Does this restlessness happen in most settings, like at work, at home, and in social situations?

Yeah, I'd say it happens pretty much everywhere. 

At work, on my shifts, I just keep moving. I go right from mopping to checking the trash to straightening chairs without really stopping. And it's the same at home. You'd think I'd want to rest after being on my feet all day, but instead of sitting down after work, I’ll just go start puttering out in the garage, or I'll end up re-sorting my tools. I just kind of stay on the go no matter where I am.
Did you have trouble staying still or sitting quietly in multiple settings when you were a child, like at school and at home?

Yeah, I did. I remember getting in trouble back in grade school for popping out of my seat all the time. I'd talk over the teacher, or I'd just start rushing ahead on things before she even finished giving the directions. And at home, well, my mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even back then. So, yeah, it's been going on since I was a kid.
When you feel restless, does it feel like you absolutely have to move and can’t keep still, or is it more that you simply prefer to stay active?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it in those terms. I don't know if I'd say I absolutely have to move, but I wouldn't really call it just a preference, either. 

It's more like... I just realize I'm already moving or fidgeting before I even think about it. I'll just be standing there and realize my foot is tapping or I'm pacing around. So I guess I'm not really sure if it's a strong need or if my body just kind of does it on its own.
When you feel that urge to move, does walking around or fidgeting make the tense feeling go away?

I'm not really sure about that, either. I don't know if I'd say I feel a specific tense feeling that goes away when I move. Like I said, it's more that I just find myself already moving. I don't really notice a build-up of tension or a sense of relief, I just... I just stay busy.
When you get up and move around, does it feel like you have an inner urge or need to move that you have to act on?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I don't... I don't feel some inner urge that I have to act on. Like I was saying, it's not really something I think about before it happens. I don't sit there feeling a need to get up, I just realize I'm already up and walking around. Or I'm already doing something else. So, no, I don't think I feel an urge like you're describing.
When you get up and move around, is it usually because you’re deliberately doing something useful or getting a task done?

Yeah, I suppose it is. I'm usually getting something done. Like on my shifts, I'll go straight from mopping the floors to checking the trash, and then I'm off to straightening up the chairs... I just do it all without really stopping. 

And it's the same thing when I get home, too. Instead of just sitting down and resting after work, I'll head out to the garage and start puttering around, or I'll end up re-sorting my tools. So, yeah, I am doing useful things, I just... I just kind of keep going.
